label: Epistemic inclusion and knowability…: Included E R requires each same-world epistemic alternative…
term: epistemic inclusion and knowability schema strength
definition: Included E R requires each same-world epistemic alternative to be a modal alternative. relationalContext constructs the existing Context with existing fixed-agent Knows E, not a new epistemic operator. GlobalForward is truth-to-possible-knowledge at all worlds; existing GlobalRestrictedEquivalence adds possible-knowledge-to-truth. AdmittedKnown concludes knowledge only for true contents in the supplied admissible family.
note: Analyst formulation for #1059, attribution deferred. E inclusion in R is not equality, commutation, time transport, factivity, or a claim that any actual possibility relation has a given structure. The universal four-world R includes E; the earlier two-block R does not. The line union includes E but is not Euclidean. World zero versus singleton world two illustrates actual ignorance versus possible knowledge. Real-world modal/epistemic applicability remains OPEN. See docs/notes/sep-fitch-knowability-gap-20261106.md.
